kicker: What managements talk about · Q4 FY26 → Q2 FY27 calls
title: Tariff talk is fading. Defence and data centres are rising.
dek: With US tariffs on India cut to 18% under the February 2026 trade deal and talks still running, tariffs came up on 22.5% of Q2 calls, down from 32.3% two quarters ago.

chart.title: Change in share of calls mentioning each theme
chart.sub: percentage points, Q2 FY27 vs Q4 FY26

stats.label: Calls discussing tariffs
stats.note: 369 calls in Q4 FY26, 306 in Q1 FY27, 254 in Q2 FY27.

stats.label: Defence indigenisation
stats.note: Mentioned on 93 Q2 FY27 calls, up from 80; mostly industrial and defence suppliers.

stats.label: Data-centre power & cooling
stats.note: 110 Q2 FY27 calls, led by electrical equipment and industrial products makers.

read: Managements have stopped explaining tariffs and started talking about where new orders come from: defence, data centres and customers moving supply chains to India.
sources: Vantage theme tracker across ~1,100 calls a quarter (BSE filings), as of 18 Nov 2026; tariff level: White House fact sheet on the US–India trade deal, Feb 2026
notes: Each call is tagged with the themes management discusses; a theme's share is the % of that quarter's calls that mention it. Shown: the six biggest risers and six biggest fallers between Q4 FY26 (calls in Apr–Jun 2026) and Q2 FY27 (Oct–Nov 2026). A mention is not a forecast: tariffs falling off calls means less discussion, not that tariff risk is gone. Open Themes on the dashboard for the companies behind each theme.
